rules: Forecasts aren't receipts: projected money never counts as observed.
Founder hours aren't free: human effort is recorded even when it costs no cash.
Old investment is not automatically a November expense: historical spend lives in its own ledger.
A released cut is immutable: later work may respond to it, never rewrite it.
Exceeding an episode's cash ceiling requires an explicit, recorded authorization.
Creative judgment, community interest and financial support are separate signals and are never summed.

payload.title: The First Transmission
payload.logline: Leonardo builds Future Radio to get funding from the future so he can finish his work.

payload.title: The People vs. The Future
payload.logline: A premortem disguised as a press conference at Milliways. Agnolo puts the season's plan on trial before it has been made.

payload.title: The Transmission Arrives
payload.summary: Leonardo's message reaches the future. Agnolo discovers the reply is a pitch deck and an invitation to Milliways.
payload.question: What did Leonardo's original investment actually create?

payload.title: Are We on Episode 2 or 10?
payload.summary: Yuria announces Episode 10 as the second broadcast. The ending arrives before the middle.
payload.question: Can an ending serve as a production plan?

payload.title: Roll Call Across Centuries
payload.summary: Shannon, Gödel, Hayek, Borges, Douglas, Leonardo, and the Creator identify their era and question.
payload.question: Which expert perspectives are actually needed?

payload.title: The Venture Capital Misunderstanding
payload.summary: Agnolo displays the historical article, highlights a pitch-deck subject, and summons it as a witness.
payload.question: What was promised, and what has actually happened?

payload.title: Slide Six's Future Profits
payload.summary: A projection claims that costs and time will fall while receipts rise. Agnolo refuses to book future outcomes as cash.
payload.question: What would count as evidence of profitability?

payload.title: The Angel Investor Mix-Up
payload.summary: A Renaissance merchant, investors, and literal angels disagree about the meaning of a return.
payload.question: What kinds of value can patrons and investors receive?

payload.title: The Artist Inside the Founder
payload.summary: Agnolo discovers the first artist using the artup is its founder. Leonardo recognizes the problem of unfinished ideas.
payload.question: Who is this technology meant to serve?

payload.title: Patrick's $250 Challenge
payload.summary: The paid $1,000 engagement meets the unresolved $250/month value test. Marvin's capabilities go on trial.
payload.question: What would make ongoing service valuable enough to renew?

payload.title: Summon Failure
payload.summary: Agnolo summons failure from November 30. Perfectionism, nobody listening, hidden labor, empty treasury, and overwhelming success testify.
payload.question: What could prevent the season from finishing?

payload.title: The Writers' Room Appears
payload.summary: The screen enters a writers' room. Borges recalls prior ideas, Leonardo helps a patron make something, and Agnolo accounts for it.
payload.question: Can patrons participate in real creative decisions?

payload.title: Before It Exists
payload.summary: An ensemble satirizes the demand to account for consequences before exploration is permitted.
payload.question: What can responsibly be known before an experiment?

payload.title: Leonardo Learns Project Management
payload.summary: Leonardo chooses eight episodes, four rounds, deadlines, budgets, selection rules, and a definition of done.
payload.question: How can the artist finish without abandoning imagination?

payload.title: Enough Time
payload.summary: The melody of Not Enough Time returns, transformed from regret about unfinished work into an acceptance of choosing.
payload.question: Can finishing something be a creative achievement?

payload.title: The Second Press Conference
payload.summary: Agnolo announces another press conference on the same episode, this time treating it as the season finale.
payload.question: How does interpretation change with context?

payload.title: A Song That Doesn't Exist Yet
payload.summary: A listener requests an unwritten song. Yuria invites them to describe it. The season's missing middle begins.
payload.question: Can the audience help create the next transmission?

payload.title: Who Is Dennis?
payload.summary: Agnolo finds an unresolved name in the old pitch documentation and adds it to the ledger.
payload.question: Which mysteries should remain open?
